correctness.rationale: For each class, verify L eigenvalues N-n_i on internal contrasts and N on weighted-zero class constants, obtaining exact effective resistances. Expanding R∘R gives the stated zero-sum quadratic identity. Cauchy–Schwarz and zero-sum mass splitting yield Στ_iw_i²≥Σw_i²/N² on W; consequently the constrained minimum exists uniquely. The bordered system determinant is nonzero, yielding m=S₂/Δ and the exact one-mode sign classification. Rank and equality vectors follow by explicit direct-sum decomposition; strictness and p* comparison use the valid finite-metric negative-type endpoint theorem. Standalone exact tests include rational inversions and Gram rank, and numeric census checks 259 profiles; they are evidence of reproducibility rather than a proof of infinity.

value.rationale: The Euclidean embeddability of electrical resistance itself is a mathematically meaningful stronger metric property than the standard sqrt-resistance Hilbert embedding. The theorem gives a closed rational decision rule for all unit complete multipartite profiles with ≥3 classes, the full centered-Gram inertia, equality-space dimension and sharp embedding rank. The at-most-one-obstruction phenomenon and opposite outcome of two equally sized/maximal-part profiles are structural, rather than routine recomputation of the known pairwise resistance table.
